question: Why do people keep familiar habits even when a smarter option is one click away?
reflection: Real progress meets people where they are, earning trust one small, useful step at a time.

sources.subject: The Grok Bot workflows worth stealing
Claude Code cuts subagent costs 99%, 6% more prompts

one_line: Shopping agents are barely being used by real customers, a reminder that convenient technology still has to beat habits that already work.

top_stories.title: Almost nobody lets agents book their rides
top_stories.what: Uber says AI agents booked only four rides and a few hundred food orders in a week when it handled hundreds of millions of trips and orders.
top_stories.why: Adoption is a behaviour problem, not a technology one: when the existing app already takes seconds, agents offer little gain, which is useful evidence for any digital service roadmap.

top_stories.title: China builds round-the-clock robot labs
top_stories.what: China is linking scientific data, AI models, computing and robotic labs that run experiments nonstop, with an early focus on drugs, materials and solar cells.
top_stories.why: National research infrastructure of this kind shows how state planning can speed up applied science, a model worth comparing with Gulf research strategies.

top_stories.title: Proof of which model answered
top_stories.what: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source prototype that produces a cryptographic proof that an answer came from a specific model, without revealing the model itself.
top_stories.why: Buyers of AI services could one day check that a vendor did not quietly swap in a cheaper model, which supports fairer public procurement.

saudi_lens.text: Saudi research bodies investing in AI for science can learn from China's approach of joining data, compute and automated labs into one national system rather than funding them separately.
Model verification tools could support procurement rules for government AI services, letting agencies confirm they receive the model they paid for.

idea.title: Why citizens skip the agent
idea.pitch: Study why people choose or avoid AI agents for routine government or commercial tasks, measuring time saved, trust and the effort of switching habits.
idea.first_step: Pick one high-volume online service and map how long each step takes today with and without an assistant.

idea_kids.title: Habit detectives
idea_kids.pitch: A short workshop where children track one daily habit for a week and design a small nudge to change it, learning why people stick to routines.
idea_kids.first_step: Design a one-page habit tracker with space for a nudge idea.

terms.definition: A laboratory where AI plans experiments and robots run them, so tests can continue day and night with little human help.
A mathematical check that confirms something is true, such as which model produced an answer, without revealing the secret details behind it.
An AI model whose internal numbers are published, so anyone can download, run and adapt it.

concepts.summary: Consumers rarely use AI agents for tasks that existing apps already make quick.
AI and robots running experiments around the clock to speed up applied research.
Proving which AI model produced an output so customers can trust what they are buying.
